newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission slow to act on tourism charges.
newsitem.headline: Commission slow to act on tourism charges.

text.p: - The European Commission was slow to act upon perceived mismanagement in its tourism directorate XXIII, a European Court of Auditors report says.

"The internal actions by the Commission with regard to irregularities identified in favour of direct actions in favour of tourism were carried out too late," the Court says in a report obtained by Reuters.

The Court said the tourism division should have informed the budgetary control directorate (DG 20) of the Commission as soon as it noticed detailed information on a dossier involving irregularities received in June 1992.
"It was only in June 1993 that they asked for DG 20's help," the report said.
The Commission's special fraud squad UCLAF -- which eventually succeeded in getting police inquiries launched in several member states in 1995, was only brought in in July 1994.
The Court also said that the Commission had not informed the Court about the irregularities and that it only fell over them by chance during an inspection.

It said that the faults and irregularities which were noticed in 1992 had still not been entirely eliminated in 1995, and therefore are preventing a three-year action plan on tourism from working properly.
It said that the Commission should strengthen selection, follow-up, evaluation and control procedures.
The tourism division has been in the spotlight since Belgian officials last January arrested two officials in connection with an investigation of bribery and fraud.

The Commission on Thursday said it had asked the German head of the division to take early retirement, but that it was not ready to lift the diplomatic immunity of Director-General Heinrich Von Moltke, as requested by Belgian authorities.
"The Commission stresses the confidence it has in the integrity and the honourability of Mr Von Moltke," Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said.
He said the move to replace Von Moltke was not linked to those two other cases and was not a reflection on Von Moltke's character. He said the Commission simply wanted to make some internal reforms.
The European Parliament's budget committee last week threatened to freeze more than a quarter of the budget for European commissioners' salaries to force them to restructure the deparment.
But van der Pas said the Commission had already been planning to make changes at the department.

The two tourism officials were arrested after investigators discovered evidence that recipients of European Union subsidies to promote tourism had paid hundreds of thousands of dollars in "illegal commissions", a Belgian anti-fraud unit said.
Those two officials were fired by the Commission, van der Pas said.
